originality.rationale: Three actual semantic published-finding corpus searches of aliases, square-zero and local Rota–Baxter ranks, together with primary source full-text comparisons, found no statement implying the entire unbounded n>=4 rank-one Segre-component and finite-field census. Closest published-finding corpus result treats a four-dimensional exterior algebra over F_2. Guo–Rosenkranz–Zheng focus on dim<=3 semigroup algebras or infinite polynomial algebra; Yu on monomial k[t] operators; the 2026 truncated-algebra title concerns a different square-zero quotient. The mathematical comparison limits the claim to the higher-length rank-one locus. Residual priority risk from unindexed general classifications is stated; absence of hits alone is not taken as proof.
residual_risks: A historical rank-one weight-zero Rota–Baxter theorem for commutative local algebras, not indexed under truncated polynomial keywords, could imply the criterion and formula.
General universal moduli descriptions might include the same Segre decomposition without using the same title.
Publication priority and geometric scheme structure are not independently certified.

value.rationale: The reduced moduli of a natural operator identity on the canonical unbounded monogenic local-algebra family gains floor(n/2) distinct geometrically irreducible Segre cones of the same dimension, with exact nested pairwise/multiple intersections. Their disjoint rank-one valuation cells admit an explicit polynomial finite-field count over every field size, providing natural geometric and arithmetic invariants beyond isolated small examples and motivating study of higher-rank Rota–Baxter loci.
